issues.failure_explanation: The energy norm contains h||grad_{n_delta}(v^e - pi_h v^e)||^2 on the hypersurface boundary. For v in H^s with s <= 3/2 the gradient has no L^2 trace on the hypersurface, so the left side can be infinite and the estimate is false or ill-defined at the lower end of the stated range. The element trace inequality used for the gradient term needs H^2 on elements.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the range to 2 <= s <= p+1 (or 3/2 < s <= p+1 with fractional trace estimates).

issues.title: Energy-norm interpolation estimate claimed for regularity range where it is false
issues.why_classification: A one-line restriction of the parameter range. No subsequent argument uses the invalid range, so no claim or rate is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $0< \delta_1 < \delta_2$ are fixed parameters independent of $\delta$ and $h$

issues.failure_explanation: u^e∘q_delta is the normal-constant extension of the trace g = u^e on ∂Ω_delta. Its H^s norm on the strip is equivalent to ||g||_{H^s(∂Ω_delta)}, which the sharp trace theorem controls only by ||u^e||_{H^{s+1/2}}, not ||u^e||_{H^s}. Composition estimates hold for diffeomorphisms, not for the projection q_delta. For example, a function in H^s whose trace on a line lies in H^{s-1/2} but not H^s has a non-H^s normal extension. The bound's constants also depend on C^{s} norms and on a reach >= delta_2 of ∂Ω_delta, uniformly in delta and h. This is never assumed and fails for the oscillatory perturbations considered, whose higher derivatives blow up like delta h^{-k alpha_n}. Hence I_1, I_{2,1}, I_{2,2}, I_{2,3} are not shown to be O(h^p)||u||_{H^{p+1}} for p >= 2 under the stated hypotheses (u in H^{p+1}, u^e in W^2_inf).

issues.failure_explanation: Since ||grad v||_{Ω_delta} <= |||v|||_h, Theorem thm:energy-error already gives an H^1-seminorm bound h^p + h^{-1/2}delta. The paper's combined result is therefore h^p + min(h^{-1/2}delta, delta + delta_n), and the 'refined' bound is sharper only if delta_n <~ h^{-1/2}delta. In the normal study (delta = h^p, delta_n ~ h^{p-alpha_n}, alpha_n = 1) and the level-set study (delta ~ h^2, delta_n ~ h, p = 2), the energy estimate predicts an H^1 rate of h^{3/2}. That is exactly the 'h^{1/2} better than predicted' rate observed. So the delta_n term cannot be sharp there without contradicting thm:energy-error, and the level-set explanation is wrong. Optimal energy convergence together with suboptimal H^1 convergence is impossible. For p = 2 with delta ~ h^2 the theory predicts energy h^{3/2} and L^2 h^2, not optimal rates 'in agreement with the analysis'.
